title: Formula versus circuit noise thresholds
formal: For p in [\(0,1/2\)), let \(Reliable(p)\) mean that there exists a constant delta>0 such that for every \(n\ge 1\) and every Boolean function \(f:\{0,1\}^{n}->\{0,1\}\), some finite circuit C of the kind below satisfies \(\Pr [C(x)=f(x)]\ge 1/2\)+delta for every input x. Is \(Reliable(p)\) true exactly for \(p<(3-\sqrt{7})/4\)? In particular, is it false at the boundary as well as above it?
definitions: A circuit is a finite directed acyclic graph with input sources \(x_{1},\ldots ,x_{n}\), constant sources 0 and 1, gates of fan-in at most two, and one designated output wire. Any Boolean function of a gate's input bits is allowed. Each gate is evaluated once in topological order and independently flips its correct Boolean output with probability exactly p. All outgoing wires from that gate carry the same resulting bit; reuse does not generate fresh independent copies. Inputs, constants, and wires are noiseless. Every computational gate, including the output gate when present, obeys the noise rule; there is no extra noiseless decoder. Fan-out is unrestricted, and different incoming paths may share gates. C may depend on p,n,f but not on x. Its size and construction time are unrestricted. The probability is solely over independent gate failures. Delta may depend on p but is common to all n,f,x. A formula is the restricted case in which computational gates have fan-out at most one, with input variables still allowed to occur repeatedly.
answer_criterion: Prove or refute the stated equivalence for the full interval \(0\le p<1/2\), including \(p=(3-\sqrt{7})/4\). A proof or refutation must use the specified independent gate-flip model and a uniform positive correctness advantage across all functions.
why: The problem asks how much unreliable local computation can be tolerated when arbitrary redundancy and reuse are available. It would determine whether sharing intermediate noisy values changes the fundamental threshold already known for formulas.

importance.reason: A sharp reliability boundary for general classical computation, separating the effects of gate errors from circuit size and design effort.

context_blocks.text: The success advantage must be fixed before choosing a function or its number of inputs. Allowing it to shrink with the function would describe a much weaker task. The noisy output itself is read, so the target does not assume an unlimited perfect final computation.

Unger establishes the exact threshold for two-input formulas, extending the earlier NAND-gate result, and conjectures the same threshold for circuits. Shared subcomputations correlate wire values even though the underlying gate failures are independent.

Later work studies asymmetric noise on AND and XOR gates and relates reliability to amplification. Its different gate-specific error assumptions and formula bounds do not settle the common-noise, unrestricted-fan-out proposition here.

progress.text: Unger proves the formula threshold \((3-\sqrt{7})/4\), including impossibility at equality, and states the circuit extension as a conjecture.
Version 5 of Shutty, Wootters, and Hayden develops asymmetric-noise results and distinguishes formulas from general circuits.

status_note: The circuit-threshold conjecture is explicit in Unger's 2008 paper. The later asymmetric-noise paper was checked as a different model. Searches through 11 September 2026 located no resolution, but did not locate a recent primary source explicitly reaffirming this exact conjecture. Historical openness should not be read as a fresh status certification.
review_note: Individually checked against the cited sources. Editorial importance is distinct from current-status evidence; no formal proof has been checked.

category_assignment.reason: The main target is the computational power of noisy Boolean circuits, rather than a channel coding rate.
